The notes further confirm the joint optimization of voxel-based radiance fields and 6-DOF camera trajectories to reconstruct blurry images.

The evidence explicitly states that the proposed method (ExBluRF) differs from DeblurNeRF, which uses 2D pixel-wise blur kernels, by formulating motion blur as a trajectory-based accumulation of rays along a Bézier curve. Specifically, the notes mention 'Reparameterize the 6-DOF camera motion trajectory for each view using a Bézier curve' and 'ExBluRF uses a trajectory-based blur model... whereas DeblurNeRF uses 2D pixel-wise spatially varying blur kernels'. The claim accurately reflects these distinctions found in the source text.

The ray origin is the camera center corresponding to $P_{\tau_i}$ [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the method accumulates colors of rays while 'the origin and the direction of the rays change along the estimated trajectory' (Section 1). Furthermore, the notes specify that intermediate sub-frame poses {P_τi} are defined from the initial to final pose, and rays r_τi(x) are generated corresponding to these intermediate camera poses. In the context of NeRF and the provided equations, the ray origin is determined by the camera position (part of the 6-DOF pose P_τi). Therefore, the claim that the ray origin corresponds to the camera center of P_τi is supported by the text.
